video_title: Can AI be a better portfolio manager than you? Why Ulys CEO Hugo Renaudin is betting on Yes
gist: Ulys CEO Hugo Renaudin pitches an AI investing assistant built on a Privy-powered self-custodial multi-chain wallet that turns natural-language worldviews into tradeable baskets of crypto and tokenized stocks, charging 1% per transaction while users sign every trade. He argues on-chain rails (24/7, global by default, tokenized stocks) are essential to the next financial app, and lays out a roadmap of prediction markets, 160-country expansion, a Q1 debit card and agentic payments.

themes.theme: Product: AI investing assistant on a self-custodial wallet

insights.claim: Ulys (rendered 'Ulysis' in the transcript) positions itself first as an AI assistant that helps users invest, with a self-custodial multi-chain wallet underneath, modeled on personal AI assistants like Meta's Muse and Instinct but specialized for investing.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Signals a category of vertical 'AI + wallet' consumer finance apps competing with brokerages and generic chatbots for retail flows.
insights.quote: Ulysis is a is an AI assistant that helps you invest

insights.claim: Ulys's core 'trade ideas' feature turns a natural-language worldview (e.g. 'I believe in data centers because of AI', DeFi, flying cars) into an AI-researched, tradeable basket of assets, aimed at people without prior financial knowledge.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Thematic, narrative-driven basket construction by retail could amplify flows into whatever themes are popular at the moment; watch for narrative-driven crowding.
insights.quote: you give it an idea about the world

insights.claim: Renaudin concedes Ulys is functionally not very different from asking ChatGPT or Claude for a recommendation and executing it in a wallet; the claimed differentiation is a single integrated experience, proactive alerts on held positions, and personalization from in-app usage data (risk tolerance, goals like buying a house in five years).
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: The moat is thin by the CEO's own admission; durability depends on proactivity, data lock-in and the tuned harness rather than model access.
insights.quote: It's not very different. It's it's basically that.

insights.claim: Ulys describes itself as 'Phantom with an AI interface': the AI prepares transactions (e.g. 'send 10 USDC to' a contact), but the user must sign and approve every trade or transfer; there is no autonomous 'YOLO mode'.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop signing keeps liability with users and limits regulatory exposure; fully autonomous agentic trading is not yet the product.
insights.quote: it's phantom with an AI interface

insights.claim: Users choose the underlying LLM themselves (e.g. Claude or ChatGPT), and Ulys says its moat is a proprietary harness and specialized tools that tune those models for investment questions, because factory-default models are 'good but not that good' at finance.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic app layers commoditize foundation models; value accrues to whoever owns the finance-specific harness and user data.
insights.quote: That's the that's our secret source is how we tailor the model

insights.claim: Ulys takes a 1% fee on every transaction, while absorbing all LLM token costs itself so AI access is free to users, citing Instinct's free model as inspiration.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: A 1% take rate is high versus zero-commission brokers; unit economics hinge on trade frequency outpacing per-user inference costs.
insights.quote: We take a 1% on every transaction.

insights.claim: Renaudin says Instinct, a WhatsApp-based AI assistant with no app or UI, is now a $30 billion company used by millions, and treats it as proof that AI quality alone is what makes such products succeed.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Benchmark valuation for consumer AI assistants; implies the market rewards assistant quality over interface.
insights.quote: now it's a $30 billion company and it's used by millions of people

insights.claim: Ulys's company is about two and a half years old: the first two years went into building the multi-chain, key-storage and gas-abstraction back end, and the AI layer was built in roughly the last year.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: AI-on-crypto apps that already solved wallet UX can bolt on AI quickly; infrastructure, not the AI, was the long pole.

insights.claim: Ulys runs with an 11-person team mixing crypto back-end engineers (including co-founders who built a Bitcoin exchange), an AI-background CTO named Dylan, and designers from Apple, Venmo and PayPal; only two people are finance-focused.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Lean team with thin finance/compliance depth is a key-person and regulatory risk to monitor.

themes.theme: Why on-chain rails for the financial app of tomorrow

insights.claim: Renaudin argues the next-generation financial app must combine AI and on-chain rails, because tokenization, real-world assets and tokenized stocks mean 'the whole world is going onchain'.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Supports the tokenized-equity/RWA thesis: consumer apps are building distribution assuming on-chain stocks become standard.
insights.quote: the whole world is going onchain

insights.claim: On-chain rails give Ulys 24/7/365 markets and international-by-default distribution: it launched in 110 (111 exact) countries simply by being a crypto wallet, a far larger addressable market than a US-only off-chain app.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Tokenized stocks let non-US fintechs reach global retail without broker licenses in each jurisdiction; distribution advantage for crypto-native apps.
insights.quote: we're live in 110 countries and that's just by virtue of being a crypto wallet

insights.claim: Renaudin predicts tokenized stocks will be used globally the way USDC is, citing French retail demand to buy Nvidia, Tesla and SpaceX exposure that is harder to access off-chain.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Watch tokenized mega-cap and pre-IPO (SpaceX) exposure demand from non-US retail as a growth driver for issuers.
insights.quote: I think tokenized stocks are going to be, you know, used everywhere in the world

insights.claim: Ulys makes available any asset on its supported chains, giving access to tokenized-stock providers there including Robinhood, Coinbase, xStocks ('XTOX') and Ondo ('Ono Tinary' in the transcript); supported chains include Bitcoin, Ethereum, Base, Solana and Robinhood chain, with Hyperliquid and others planned by year-end.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Aggregator apps route retail flow to whichever tokenized-stock issuer lives on supported chains; Robinhood chain inclusion is a notable distribution point.

insights.claim: A single Ulys basket can span chains, e.g. some Bitcoin, tokenized Nvidia on Robinhood chain and ETH elsewhere, with the AI choosing chains and the user never needing to know the product is multi-chain.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Chain abstraction makes underlying chain choice invisible to users, shifting competition to liquidity and asset availability.
insights.quote: a bit of you know tokenized Nvidia on Robin Hood

insights.claim: Ulys outsources wallet infrastructure and key security to Privy: users log in with email or phone, which generates a self-custodial key recoverable through Privy, and keys can be exported to MetaMask or Phantom; Ulys says it stores no keys.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Embedded-wallet providers like Privy are becoming the default plumbing for consumer crypto apps; concentration risk sits with them.
insights.quote: You can withdraw your you can take your private key and generate it on MetaMask or Phantom.

insights.claim: Renaudin's design principle is that Ulys 'is a crypto app, but it shouldn't feel like a crypto app': users fund with debit/credit card or Apple Pay, and seed-phrase and multi-chain complexity is hidden.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Abstraction of crypto UX is the key unlock for mainstream onboarding; apps that succeed here can capture non-crypto-native retail.
insights.quote: Ulys is a crypto app, but it it shouldn't feel like a crypto app

insights.claim: Ulys does no KYC itself, but its fiat on-ramp and forthcoming debit-card providers do; Renaudin says the company may eventually centralize KYC as third-party partners multiply.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Regulatory perimeter is pushed onto partners for now; a shift to in-house KYC would signal regulatory pressure or scale.

insights.claim: Without KYC, Ulys enforces geographic restrictions on tokenized stocks (e.g. Robinhood tokenized stocks being unavailable to US users) using App Store region, phone location and IP address, and the AI routes users to an allowed alternative.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Geofencing via app-store/IP is a soft compliance control that regulators may test; jurisdictional access shapes which issuers win retail flow.

insights.claim: Renaudin argues an AI-powered wallet is less risky than a normal wallet for picking assets and avoiding scams, because the AI can check liquidity and the official contract address of a memecoin on the fly, whereas humans are easily fooled; hallucinated or mismatched baskets remain the main AI risk.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: If AI vetting reduces scam losses, it is a selling point; but hallucination risk with real money remains unresolved and is a liability vector.
insights.quote: in terms of like buying the right asset or you know like avoiding scams I think AI is is more safe

insights.claim: Because the user validates every transaction, Renaudin says responsibility for bad AI-recommended trades sits with the user, though Ulys accepts a responsibility to make recommendations good; the AI is also tasked with flagging risks such as low liquidity or high volatility and offering swaps.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Liability framing for AI financial advice is untested; watch for regulatory treatment of AI recommendations as investment advice.

insights.claim: Ulys plans to add prediction markets by year-end, framing them as another way to trade a worldview alongside stocks and tokens.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Another consumer distribution channel for prediction markets; reinforces convergence of prediction markets with retail investing apps.
insights.quote: We want to add prediction markets to the app as well

insights.claim: Ulys targets expansion from 111 to about 160 countries by year-end; it is live in the US, most of South America and some of Asia, with Europe coming in a second release.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Europe launch is a catalyst to watch given MiCA-era rules and French founder roots.

insights.claim: Ulys plans a debit card likely in Q1 next year and a broader push into payments, including agentic payments where AI optimizes purchases (e.g. picking the cheapest acceptable sweater), toward a 'super intelligent money app' that also offers in-app yield.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Agentic payments are an emerging battleground; AI wallets moving into card spend compete with neobanks.
insights.quote: The vision is to have a an you know a money app like a super intelligent money app.

insights.claim: Renaudin predicts that within five years people will use separate AI agents for work, personal life and finances, and that the financial agent will be a distinct app because it needs different data and connections; Ulys aims to be that default financial agent.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Supports a thesis that vertical AI agents (not one general assistant) capture finance; vertical data and integrations are the moat.
insights.quote: we're going to have agents for our financial life

insights.claim: Renaudin's thesis is that most ordinary people have good ideas about the world but cannot translate them into investments, and AI can bridge that gap and democratize investing by stripping out financial jargon and complexity.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: If AI-driven thematic retail investing scales, expect more narrative-driven retail flows into thematic baskets and tokenized assets.
insights.quote: most people don't know how to translate that idea of the world into something that they can invest

insights.claim: A new, smarter and more proactive version of Ulys's AI is expected within the next couple of weeks, with the remainder of the year focused on AI recommendation quality rather than new features, leveraging more user data.
insights.speaker: Hugo Renaudin (Ulys CEO)
insights.so_what: Near-term product catalyst; signals the company sees AI quality, not breadth, as the competitive lever.
